subject: Food Science
title: Refrigeration Changed Everything
description: A 60-second lesson on Refrigeration Changed Everything.

hook.text: Before mechanical refrigeration (1876), New York City dumped 150,000 tons of horse manure daily.

buildup.text: Frederic Tudor ('The Ice King') shipped lake ice from Boston to the Caribbean in the 1830s—insulated with sawdust.

discovery.text: Carl von Linde invented the compression refrigerator in 1876—using ammonia. For the first time, cold could be created anywhere.

twist.text: Refrigerated railcars (1880s) transformed the US diet overnight. Midwestern beef reached East Coast cities fresh.

climax.text: Home refrigerators became common by the 1940s. Before that, Americans shopped for food daily.

punchline.text: From lake ice to ammonia compressors. Refrigeration ended daily shopping, enabled cities.

quiz.question: How did refrigerated railcars change the American diet?
options: Midwestern beef could reach East Coast cities fresh—ending reliance on salt-preserved local meat
